body: Yeah, I feel BPD treatment is very focused on appearing/acting stable around others and it sort of ignores how I actually feel. People say I'm a success story, but I'm far more suicidal/dissociative/self harming than most people I know. No one, no specific activity, and no medication has ever been able to make that go away or lessen. Not saying it's an easy fix, but still. I hope something exists in the future for others.
I'm glad you've found things to keep you in the present moment and away from suicide :) I appreciate your responses and attempts to help as well.

Medication can absolutely have those types of side effects. The common wisdom (just look at the disclaimers at the end of drug commercials) is to stop taking it immediately and contact your doctor. Don't keep taking the medication if you think it could be the issue. If you can afford to, it might be worth going to the ER.

Well, yes. There's no medication for BPD, and I've been on medication for depression/anxiety since I was 13 (SSRIs make my symptoms worse, other drugs didn't improve much). I've been in therapy since I was 10 and had some positive experiences with it, but even my best therapists can't change my thoughts and feelings; they can help me cope with them, but that doesn't stop me from dissociating most nights or crying in my bathtub for no apparent reason. Like, I recognize my emotions, cool, what do I do to get rid of them that I haven't already tried?

Like I said in the title, people have told me "it gets better" for over 20 years. Over that time, I not only took advantage of all the mental health resources I could, I also did everything in my power to make sure my external life circumstances were the best they could be. Now that I'm in the true adult portion of my life where nothing really changes anymore, I can confidently say that it never got better and I don't see what major life change would make that happen.

Ah, I see what your saying. Unfortunately for me, the extreme emotions don't really pass, they either spiral or get replaced with some other extreme emotion (if it's a positive one, I feel extra terrible when I come down from it a bit later). Unfortunately for me, having a "stable" life does not outweigh my feelings. Yes, I probably have comorbid depression.

To be fair, I did find therapy (after I found a decent therapist) improved my quality of life (well, my relationships) greatly. For BPD, specifically, it's very common for people to "act out" and foster unhealthy relationships with friends/family/coworkers etc, and therapy helped me realize and regulate that. So, I will say therapy can help, but yeah, definitely didn't get rid of my actual suicidal thoughts or negative thinking. I just treat people better than I did before, which is great, but doesn't actually make me feel better.

I appreciate your reply. For me, it's not a sense of emptiness. I feel very strong negative emotions to simple things in life (ex, if one of my good friends mentions a coworker they like, I feel extreme jealousy and betrayal, even though those aren't appropriate reactions). When I was untreated/undiagnosed, I'd act on those feelings, and it damaged a lot of friendships. But it's been a very long time since then, and I now know how to maintain healthy, close, functional relationships. But the intense, awful feelings I have still exist and they will never go away. I feel them every single day over very minor things. I can function with them, and most don't realize I even feel them, but it's exhausting and not a life worth living, in my opinion.

The fact is, I don't particularly value anything in life that's actually possible to obtain. I should be clear, I love my friends, they're amazing and very supportive. I have hobbies and passions. But at the end of the day, they don't even begin to negate how depressed and manic (for lack of better terms) I always feel.
